chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who marries a woman for temporary marriage (mut'ah); is it permissible for him to marry her daughter? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan, a title referring to Imam al-Rida (AS) or Imam al-Jawad (AS) depending on the source context, here used as the authority for the ruling.
key_terms.مُتْعَةً: Temporary marriage (mut'ah), a form of marriage with a specified duration and dowry.
key_terms.يَحِلُّ: Permissible (halal), indicating legal allowance in Islamic jurisprudence.

ai.seo_question: Is a man permitted to marry the daughter of his temporary wife in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the kinship by marriage (muhrim) established through temporary marriage (mut'ah) is sufficient to prohibit marrying the daughter, mirroring the rules of permanent marriage. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it confirms that the contractual bond of mut'ah creates a real, not merely nominal, relationship of affinity, thereby extending the prohibition of mahram to the daughter. The hadith underscores the consistency of marital prohibitions across both forms of marriage recognized in Shia law.
